items.title: jjfx
items.author: Curator
items.content:
jjfx is a terminal interface for managing Jujutsu workspaces and the agents working in them inside of the terminal.

This tool's workspace list groups work by status and opens a commit graph or the selected workspace's diff. Keyboard actions create and remove workspaces, fetch changes, rebase work and resolve conflicts. A worker pool dispatches tickets or written tasks to agents in separate workspaces.

jjfx exposes commands for dispatch, review and delivery, with JSON status output for scripts. Dispatch avoids workspaces already open in a terminal and refuses uncertain cases unless forced.

This too is best used by developers that are using Jujutsu who want to review parallel changes and coordinate with agent work across multiple workspaces.

items.title: bootvine
items.author: Curator
items.content:
bootvine is a terminal tool that shows which systemd startup services are being initialized in the Linux system after startup and shutdown.

It shows a live tree timeline of which services are still starting and what they are currently waiting for. The timeline gives details of which services took the longest (in seconds) or failed and which ones appear with their error messages and recent logs.

The tree shows services which belong at which stage of the loading process and it gives a short description of what the service does. bootvine is runs on Linux systems that use systemd and can show the earliest stage of startup if that stage uses systemd too.

bootvine is very useful to Linux users who want to find out which systemd services are delaying startup or shutdown, see what those services are waiting for and to easily investigate why something fails without scrolling through the kernel and systemd logs.

items.title: rail
items.author: Curator
items.content:
rail is a terminal email client for reading and sending mail through Gmail and Microsoft 365.

It combines accounts in one inbox and keeps messages in a local SQLite store for reading and searching. It also supports saved searches, snoozing and bulk actions, so several conversations can be archived, moved or marked as read together.

Messages are written in your preferred editor, then reviewed with their attachments before sending. Drafts stay on your computer until you choose to save them to your account, and a ten-second delay gives you time to cancel a send.

rail runs on Linux and macOS and is for developers and system administrators who prefer managing personal and work email alongside their other terminal tools.

items.title: jotter
items.author: Curator
items.content:
jotter is a terminal-based Jupyter notebook editor that can run notebooks and renders LaTeX math formulas and plots in your terminal.

It can open regular Jupyter notboook files (.ipynb) and after running code in the notebook, it displays its output and supports displaying inline LaTeX formulas drawn as Kitty Graphics, Sixel or iTerm2 image format depending on your terminal. It can also display inline animated matplotlib figures and renders are designed to have fast feedback loops.

Notebook edits are auto-saved and jotter's editor deals with crash recovery which protects unsaved edits to pick up where you left off. Vim key-bindings are supported in the editor (if you are familiar with Vim mode navigation) and you can also use jotter to load from any virtualenv setup.

This tool is very useful towards students, machine learning developers, researchers or anyone looking for alternative Jupyter notebook editors that can open full notebooks and inspect their live results in of a terminal with inline fast rendering.

items.title: tennis
items.author: Curator
items.content:
tennis is a command-line tool that displays CSV or TSV and other structured data in the form of formatted terminal tables.

The columns can be auto-resized to fit the terminal dimensions and it truncates long cells and formats numeric values. It can be customized in how it displays the data such as choosing the colors to match the background or the border styles.

tennis can also be used as a CLI and accepts JSON, JSONL and SQLite data as input alongside other delimited files. It has a peak mode to summarize the data shape and column contents if you prefer to avoid viewing all the data in one table.

This terminal tool is useful to developers who need an alternative CSV viewer that is cross platform, can inspect beyond CSV files and is composable via piping command output for automation.

items.title: rmlint
items.author: Curator
items.content:
rmlint is a command-line tool that scans directories for duplicate files and other filesystem files.

It compares file contents to identify duplicates, with filters for size and modification time. It can find files that are empty, have broken symbolic links or files that have invalid ownership permissions.

By default, a scan leaves the scanned files untouched and writes a shell script for review. You can choose which copies to keep and configure the script to delete duplicates or replace them with hard links or symbolic links. It can deal with caching so that it saves time in searching again until there is a difference in the file.

rmlint is for users such as system administrators, developers and archivists who need a tool to reclaiming space and find duplicate files in large file collections or checking an old backup drive for files already stored elsewhere.
